title: Add tenant-aware incremental migration state machine and retention-aware backups
author: Asha Kapoor
release_notes:
- Introduces tenant-aware incremental migration state machine to support pausable, resumeable schema+data upgrades for on-prem deployments.
- Adds retention-aware backup policy and restore verifier to minimize on-disk retention while ensuring rollback safety.
- Helm chart values and Terraform module updates to opt in to incremental migrations and per-tenant backup retention.
- No breaking API changes; migrations opt-in via chart/TF flags.
body:
Context and motivation:
Large on-prem/private customers with many tenants and strict maintenance windows hit operational limits with monolithic migration jobs. Full-DB migrations take hours and amplify rollback risk. This PR implements an incremental, tenant-aware migration state machine plus retention-aware backup/restore flows so upgrades can progress tenant-by-tenant, be paused/resumed, and verified at each step. Goal: reduce blast radius, shorten maintenance windows, and enable safe automated rollbacks.

What this changes (high level):
- New migration controller (go/incremental/migration_state_machine) that tracks per-tenant migration progress, retries, and backoff.
- Backup Manager additions (go/backup/retention_manager) implementing size- and age-based retention policies and soft-delete markers with TTL.
- New Helm chart flags (charts/redwood-private/values.yaml) to enable incremental migrations and to configure per-tenant backup retention and concurrency.
- Terraform module (terraform/modules/private_installer) add opt-in variables and migration plan output for operators.
- CLI helpers: rwctl migration plan / rwctl migration resume / rwctl backup verify (scripts/cli/).
- Small schema migration helper library (go/migrations/util) to register reversible steps and checksum metadata for downgrade safety.

Checklist / rollout plan: 
- [x] Unit tests for state machine transitions and retention decisions.
- [x] Integration test that runs a simulated multi-tenant migration with pause/resume.
- [x] E2E restore verification workflow validated in staging.
- [x] Helm/Terraform docs added to `docs/private/upgrade_playbook.md`.
- [x] Add a feature flag: `migration.incremental.enabled` (default: false).
- [x] Migration hooks emit audit events for operator visibility.

Commits (summary):
- feat(migration): add tenant-state-machine and transition scheduler
- feat(backup): retention manager and soft-delete TTL markers
- feat(helm,tf): add flags and outputs for incremental migrations
- feat(cli): rwctl helpers for plan/resume/verify
- fix(tests): stabilize integration flakiness and timeouts

Files/areas changed (high level):
- go/incremental/migration_state_machine.go (+420)
- go/backup/retention_manager.go (+300)
- charts/redwood-private/values.yaml (+12)
- terraform/modules/private_installer/variables.tf (+50)

- docs/private/upgrade_playbook.md (+220)

Key technical details and design notes: 
- State machine stores minimal per-tenant cursor (tenant_id, last_applied_migration, status, last_checkpoint_checksum) in the installer control plane DB. This keeps memory footprint bounded and avoids long-lived locks on customer DBs.
- Each migration step registers a reversible operator plus an idempotent verification function; verification runs after each tenant batch and must pass before advancing.
- Backups are created with a deterministic manifest that includes a 256-bit checksum per table/snapshot. Restore verifier replays checksums against restored artifacts to detect bit-rot or partial restores before toggling traffic.
- Retention policy supports: max_disk_bytes, min_retention_days, and per-tenant overrides. Soft-delete markers allow immediate logical deletion while keeping a short TTL for quick rollback scenarios.
- Rollback path: controller will attempt automated downgrade by applying registered reverse steps per-tenant. If reverse steps are not registered, operator is required to run manual rollback playbook; we include safe-guarding flags to disallow downgrade unless `migration.allow_downgrade` is true.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Miguel Torres (reviewer): "Please ensure we have an e2e path that exercises restore verifier under simulated corruption. Also suggest adding a metric for 'migration_pauses' to surface operator interventions."
- Asha (author reply): "Added integration test in tests/integration/migration_corruption_test.go and exported migration_pauses counter to the metrics registry. See commit 4efb3a9."
- Lin Zhao (reviewer): "Docs need a step-by-step operator checklist for partial failures; add example rwctl commands and sample outputs."
- Asha: "Expanded docs/private/upgrade_playbook.md with rwctl examples and a section on 'unsafe states' and recommended operator actions."
- Priya Singh (reviewer): "CI failed on lint in first run; after fixing codegen formatting and adding linters for yaml, re-run succeeded. Approving pending green CI."

CI summary:
- Initial CI run: build passed, unit tests passed, integration timed out on one test (fixed - increased timeout and stabilized test harness). Lint failed (yaml formatting) -> author fixed.
- Final CI: all checks passed (unit, integration, e2e migration corruption test, lint, helm lint).

Backward/rollback safety and downgrade guards:
- Migrations include checksum metadata per-step; if checksum mismatch is detected during resume, the controller halts and marks tenant state as ERROR.
- Controller will not attempt automatic downgrade unless `migration.allow_downgrade=true` is explicitly set in Helm/TF. This flag requires operator confirmation in rwctl before proceeding.
- Documentation includes recovery playbook for tenants in ERROR state, and operators can run `rwctl migration resume --force` after manual inspection.

Operational notes for operators: 
- Enable `migration.incremental.enabled` in staging, run `rwctl migration plan --concurrency 2` to preview workload.
- Monitor metrics: `migration_progress{tenant}`, `migration_pauses`, `backup_retention_bytes_used`.
- Recommended retention defaults: min_retention_days=7, max_disk_bytes per-tenant=10GB (tunable).

Merge outcome: 
- Approved by: Miguel Torres, Lin Zhao, Priya Singh.
- CI: green.
- Merge method: squash and merge. Commit message normalized to: "Add tenant-aware incremental migration state machine and retention-aware backups (ENG-1982, ENG-2024)"

Follow-ups (tracked in ENG- series):
- ENG-2101: Add UI visibility to show per-tenant migration cursors in Console.
- ENG-2102: Metrics-driven autoscaling for migration controller to increase concurrency during low-traffic windows.
- ENG-2110: Add cross-region replication safety checks for private deployments using multi-site backups.

Notes on uniqueness and divergence from previous work: 
This PR is intentionally focused on an incremental state machine and retention-aware backups rather than the purely atomic snapshot/restore or manifest-hash locking approaches in prior changes. It targets operational practicality for large multi-tenant private deployments where upgrades must be staged, paused, and resumed without forcing long downtimes or large retention footprints.

If there are follow-up concerns about the on-disk manifest format or verification algorithms, I can open a separate RFC to standardize the manifest schema across installers and the hosted control plane.
